This appeal coming on for admission this day, the Court   following:

ORDER This is the repeat (second) criminal appeal filed by the appellant under Section 14-A of the SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act against the impugned order dated 25/11/2022 passed by Special Judge (Atrocities) Act, District Burhanpur (M.P.), whereby the Court below has dismissed the application filed by the appellant under Section 439 Cr.P.C for grant of bail.
His first criminal appeal (Cr.A. No.11179/2022) was dismissed as withdrawn vide order dated 04/01/2023.

sentences.text:
The appellant is in custody since 21/11/2022 relating to FIR No.519/2022 dated (not mentioned)
registered at Police Station Shikarpura, District Burhanpur (M.P.) for the offences mentioned therein.

As per the prosecution, a complaint was lodged by the complainant that the present appellant has harassed and threatened her to do rajinama in an earlier matter which was registered against the present appellant on the complaint of the complainant under Sections 376, 376 (2)(n) and 190 of IPC.
Learned counsel for the appellant submits that the appellant has been falsely implicated.
Earlier the complainant has filed an application for cancellation of bail which was dismissed, hence, she has taken this innovative idea of making a false case against him.
It is submitted that the appellant has remained under custody for nearly 5 months now and the trial is going to take a long time, under the circumstances, he may be released on bail.
Considering the fact that the appellant is under custody for the last 5 months, this criminal appeal is allowed.

It is directed that appellant shall be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rs. Fifty Thousand only) with one surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court, for his presence before the said Court on all the dates of hearing fixed in this regard during the trial.
It is further directed that the appellant shall also comply with the provisions of Section 437(3) of Cr.P.C.
It is further directed that the appellant shall cooperate in the trial and appear before the trial Court as and when he is required.

In case, if any other complaint is filed against him while he is on bail or during the pendency of the trial or if any attempt is made by him to influence or threaten the witnesses, directly or indirectly, this bail order shall stand cancelled automatically.
Let a copy of this order be also sent to the counsel for the State for information and compliance.
Certified copy as per rules.
(NANDITA DUBEY) JUDGE sjk Ajay vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 21 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/153171731/
